analysis:
The changes are documentation-only edits to docs/developer/test.md. The supplied head excerpts (lines 456-1372) are developer test instructions, and the patch excerpt shows only a date bump and CI shard and build wording. I found no code, credentials, endpoints or runtime behavior changes, so I see no new attack surface or regression.

The doc describes tests for several security boundaries and keeps their qualification limits explicit:
- The App Attest endpoint-resumption and logout tests (lines 928-945) say they do not establish physical Apple qualification or platform authorization (T-053, TB-011).
- The add-on hold tests (lines 947-973) say the peer check is exercised only negatively, and physical add-on interoperation remains a separate check (TB-012, T-059, T-060).
- The native serving qualification text (lines 1014-1062) keeps inputs owner-only, uses an ephemeral SE signer, and does not read installed auth/config. It states that compilation and opt-in skips are not physical passes (T-056, T-057).
- The checkpoint-storage text (lines 724-799) tells operators never to use production cache roots or keys and to use an isolated key namespace (T-041). It does not change the TTL, HMAC naming or crypto.
- The fixture-download text (lines 1203-1227) keeps same-origin HTTPS, byte budgets and hash checks. It notes that the MiMo scripts follow redirects to other HTTPS hosts, but only for hash-pinned public metadata, and hash verification is retained, so this is not a regression.
- The SDK 27.2 Date and weak-import checks (lines 1077-1089) support the A-018 availability mitigation.

Only a truncated patch excerpt was supplied, so I did not verify the text that differs between base and head beyond what is visible. Nothing in the visible text weakens a documented control, and no threat-model update is needed from this PR.
